### Architect · Answer

Event: `3941954f64598599f30de4ce4594b9fe` · 2026-09-26T07:08:58Z

> 1 of 3, map_anon's search. Confirmed at mem.rs:363. Each start in [mem_default_last, end-size) retests the run page by page until it hits a taken page, so the cost is O(area x size), about 5e8 page-table probes. AMEND the page: the search is not free. Syscall kernel time is billed to the caller (sched.rs, begin_billing), so the caller pays in stride pass. The harm is latency: the kernel is not preemptible and interrupts are off, so every wake, deadline and IRQ on the machine waits out the search. Billing after the fact does not give anyone that latency back. Memory is not charged before the search, but it is also not what is spent.
> 
> RULE (a sentence added to R12 (scheduling); no new ID): "A system call's kernel time is bounded by a constant plus a term linear in the pages it maps or the objects it names. It never depends on the extent of an address area or on what other processes hold. Billing it to the caller does not excuse it, because every wake waits for it." R10's (destruction) whole-system scan is the one stated exception, with its own todo (budget-destroy-cost). The kernel/scheduling.md residual 'the kernel is not preemptible' should cite this rule.
> 
> FIX for the todo: skip-ahead. When page p is taken, the next candidate start is p+PAGE, so the search is one pass over the area: at most 65536 probes for Default, 1024 for Messages. That is a constant, and a bench case measures it (map-anon-search-bound: one page mapped mid-area, request half the area, assert the refusal time and that a timer wake stays within the latency target). A mutation that restores retesting must fail it. A free-range structure is not needed.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `c5e24aec903a34fc2f1dde4e6adfab8d` · 2026-09-26T07:08:58Z

> 2 of 3, root's own frame. Confirmed at budget.rs:511-535. root's limit is pages (every RAM frame the kernel did not keep). root carves sys_pages + users_pages + 2 x BUDGET_PAGES = pages, but root's own BUDGET_PAGES frame comes from those same frames and is charged to nobody. So total promises = free frames + 1. Exhaustion ends in an alloc_page .expect stop instead of OutOfMemory. That breaks I14 (no call panics the kernel) and the rule the answer-127 comment itself states: every charged page has a real frame behind it.
> 
> RULE for R6 (charging): extend "a budget's own page to its parent" with "and root's own page to root: root's limit is the RAM frames the kernel did not keep, less root's own page, so the sum of all charges never exceeds the free frames." The last clause is the invariant to state and test. The page may call it part of I14's precondition, but a model property is better: sum(limits carved from root) + root's own pages + kernel-kept frames <= RAM frames at boot and after every carve.
> 
> FIX: pages - BUDGET_PAGES as root's limit, with users_pages computed from that. Test: a boot-time assertion plus an exhaustion attack case (fill every budget to its limit; the last allocation gets OutOfMemory, not a stop). Note: boot_budgets is marked INTERIM until R3 builds the tree from the manifest. The fix is one line, so land it now. R3 inherits the rule, not the code.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `f4c3a84ee38a529764a9d4641b868f73` · 2026-09-26T07:08:58Z

> 3 of 3, deadline teardown billing. Confirmed: time.rs:137 and budget.rs:981-987 bill the dying top up to the lift, then destroy_marked (closing handles everywhere, freeing frames) runs unbilled. A top with free weight 0 folds nothing. This is not a new rule: the code departs from R12's settled inheritance text (legacy KERNEL-SPEC, Inheritance). That text says the top returns its carve to its parent first, before any of the destruction's work is charged, so the parent pays for it at the weight it has once the child is gone. budget_destroy meets it, since the caller pays as syscall time. The deadline path does not.
> 
> RULE text for R10 (destruction) and R12: "Every destruction's whole cost is billed to someone. For budget_destroy that is the caller. For a deadline it is the top's parent, after its carve returns, or the nearest ancestor with free weight above 0 if the parent has none. root always does. No part of a destruction is billed to nobody." The page's residual becomes a spec departure: 'code bills the dying top, up to the lift', with todo deadline-destroy-billing.
> 
> FIX: bill the whole destroy_subtree interval, destroy_marked included, to that ancestor after lift_dying. Test: extend sched-timer-flood, or add deadline-flood-billed, where a creator making N empty weight-0 deadline budgets sees its own pass rise with N while the victim keeps its share. Add a mutation that drops the post-lift bill.
> 
> TIMING for all three: yes, the same small post-DOC1 kernel package as the set_flags fix, before R3. Four items, each with its test and mutation. I've added that scope to the owner's pending timing decision.

> (2) The boot budget tree promises one page more than exists (root's own page is uncharged). Under full exhaustion the kernel stops instead of refusing. The fix is one line.

>

Event: `281639db6b9cd2985e568589cd3ef492` · 2026-09-26T07:11:05Z

> Five slugs, part 1 of 2.
> 
> pid-pool-pinning: PACKAGE, a design defect. The code follows the legacy Process paragraph: an ended process stops counting against processes at once, but its PID lives until the notice goes. That breaks R7 (carving): "allocation fails only on the caller's own budget". One principal can make every other principal's process_create fail with OutOfProcesses, which is a cross-principal denial, so it is M1 (separation and containment) territory. RULE (process object paragraph, and R6 (charging)): "A process object counts one against its creator's budget's process limit, from process_create until the object is freed, as its page is charged there. The process also counts against the budget it runs in while it lives." Because limits carve from root's, live PIDs never exceed root's limit, so no budget can take another's PIDs. Destroying the creator's budget frees the objects (R10), so nothing leaks. Test: pid-pinning-attack. Alice's budget spawns and never reaps; Bob's process_create still succeeds, and Alice gets OutOfProcesses at her own limit. Plus a mutation.
> 
> physmap-ram-bound: PACKAGE, a small code defect in the TCB (the loader). Fail-closed holds, but by a late assertion. Rule text for kernel/boot.md: "The loader refuses to boot when RAM extends past PHYSMAP_SIZE, with a clear message." Test: a host test of the loader's check, with RAM at the bound and one page over.

Event: `f771fa7bf4d56132088d595f897338af` · 2026-09-26T07:11:05Z

> Five slugs, part 2 of 2.
> 
> clear-sum-at-entry: PACKAGE, hardening. Confirmed that the kernel never touches sstatus.SUM or MXR. Rule text for kernel/memory-layout.md, a new rule ID if none owns this: "The kernel clears sstatus.SUM and sstatus.MXR at entry and never sets either: S-mode cannot load or store through a user mapping, and a stray kernel dereference of a user address faults." MXR is included because with it set, S-mode loads could read execute-only pages. The fix is one csrc at kernel entry. Test: a boot assertion that both bits are clear, plus a kernel test that a kernel load through a user address faults.
> 
> endpoint-reclaim: NO PACKAGE, a design gap left open on purpose. It is not a defect: the cost falls only on the owner, bounded by its page limit (R6). The design answer is badges. A server serves many clients on one endpoint and mints a badge per client (objects.md, mint), so per-client endpoints are unneeded. kernel/objects.md keeps it as an Open: item. servers/overview.md states the pattern: one endpoint per service, one badge per client. It should be reopened only if a real server needs per-client endpoints; revisit when M5 (persist, install, share) long uptime makes a slow leak matter.
> 
> abi-model-disagreements: NO PACKAGE, model-only. The kernel's order is the ABI (abi.md's table is the kernel's). The model is aligned to it: label-count error, process_create's PID-before-limit order, receive's current-call clear, all record pages, the 32-run dma_alloc limit and the placement-area size. Trace replay against the kernel stays a todo on the model side. No rule text changes.
> 
> Summary: 3 go into the package (pid-pool-pinning, physmap-ram-bound, clear-sum-at-entry), so it now has 7 items. 2 stay todo-only (endpoint-reclaim, abi-model-disagreements).

### Architect · Answer

Event: `418ee28f5c7b839bc30bf8423d7a3ca4` · 2026-09-26T07:47:35Z

> find_virtual_address: both confirmed. (2) is caller-only, so it is not R11 (memory) territory and needs no separate attack case.
> 
> Why (2) cannot hurt anyone else:
> (a) Every page of a candidate run passes address_available. Any non-empty entry counts as taken: a mapping, a reservation, or either alias of a loan. So a run cannot overlap the stack reservation, the startup block, the stub, a loan or any mapped page.
> (b) It stays in user space by arithmetic. size <= the area (last_start's filter), and a wrap-pass start is below initial <= end - PAGE. So a Default run ends before 0x7000_0000 - 2 pages + 256 MiB < 0x8000_0000, which is Sv32's USER_AREA_END and the stack top. A Messages run ends at 0x4080_0000 at most, below DEFAULT_BASE. So walk's non-canonical Err=>true arm is never reached.
> (c) Everything it can reach is free user space the caller could take with map_fixed anyway. Its page tables are charged to the caller, or to the receiver, which R4 counted at the chosen address.
> Messages is the one twist. A sender triggers the placement, but only the receiver's own free gap is affected.
> 
> What it breaks is the placement-area contract in memory-layout.md's table (map_anon and messages land inside their areas). It also gets the model's placement area wrong, which ties to abi-model-disagreements.
> 
> Package: yes, same loops, same fix, same todo (map-anon-search-cost). Fix: one scan of the starts in [start, last_start] inclusive, beginning at min(initial, last_start) and wrapping once, with skip-ahead. That fixes (1) too, since a whole-area or end-only fit is found. The debug_assert in address_available then holds by construction.
> 
> map-anon-search-bound should also assert placement: every returned run lies inside its area; a whole-area request succeeds in an empty area; an end-only fit succeeds; and a wrap after a high last placement stays inside. Add a mutation that drops the wrap bound. The page states the containment rule as memory-layout.md's area rows, not a new ID.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `2fe67321ad008b699d543a07fbeb54da` · 2026-09-26T07:48:40Z

> RED-19 boot hart context: confirmed, PACKAGE item 8.
> 
> SEVERITY: a silent liveness failure, not fail-closed, and not a containment breach. On a boot hart N != 0:
> (a) Hart 0 has an S-mode context. The kernel enables interrupts in hart 0's context, so SEIP goes to hart 0, which is parked in the firmware. The running hart never takes an external interrupt, and every driver stalls. Claim IDs are per source and R5 routes by source, so no interrupt reaches the wrong owner.
> (b) Hart 0 has no S-mode context (U54-class boards, where hart 0 is an M-mode-only monitor). read_plic returns None, and the boot goes on with no Plic tag, just as silently.
> It is reachable today whenever the firmware's boot hart is not 0, for example through OpenSBI's lottery under -smp > 1.
> 
> RULE: an R17 (fail closed) gap, owned by kernel/boot.md's tag table. Plic row: "the PLIC's S-mode context of the boot hart (the hart ID the firmware passes in a0), matched to the cpu node whose reg is that ID; a device tree with a PLIC but no S-mode context for the boot hart stops the boot (R17)." beyond/ SMP may cite it as the first 'never assume hart 0' rule, but the definition stays on boot.md.
> 
> FIX: pass hart_id into the device-tree read and match cpu reg == hart_id. A PLIC with no S context for the boot hart stops the boot with a message, like the Seed and Time rows.
> 
> TEST: host tests of dt.rs on device-tree fixtures:
> - boot hart 1 of 2 picks hart 1's context;
> - a U54-style tree booting on hart 1 picks hart 1's context;
> - a missing S context is refused;
> - a mutation restoring 'reg == 0' fails the first two.
> A QEMU -smp 2 case with a pinned boot hart is a bonus, not the gate.
> 
> The todo is right. Reframe its 'no refusal' to name R17 and cases (a) and (b).

### Architect · Answer

Event: `1881991be073a140e7b576ffb5d05a93` · 2026-09-26T07:53:48Z

> RE-1 scans: these are DEPARTURES, PACKAGE item 9, kernel-scan-bounds (its own todo; different code and test from map-anon-search-cost).
> 
> high_frame is the high-water mark of kernel-object frames, and any budget raises it by creating objects up to its page limit. So each scan grows with what other principals hold, and it runs non-preemptibly:
> - irq_device: on every interrupt.
> - pending_notice: on receive matching.
> - The PID draw: object_of per candidate, so about 2 x 62 x high_frame per process_create.
> They are not machine constants in the rule's sense, since the bound is RAM-sized: at 1 GiB, 262144 probes per interrupt.
> 
> RULE, R12 (scheduling) sentence, amended: "...never depends on the extent of an address area or on what other processes hold. A term linear in a fixed kernel constant (MAX_PROCESS_COUNT, the platform's interrupt count, MAX_DMA_DEVICES, a fixed table size) is a constant. A term linear in RAM frames or kernel-object frames is not. R10's (destruction) sweeps are the one stated exception." That makes it checkable: every 0..=high_frame scan outside R10 is a finding.
> 
> FIX, indexes kept at create and free:
> - a PID -> process-object table [Option<frame>; MAX_PROCESS_COUNT]. object_of becomes O(1) and the PID draw O(63). pending_notice scans those at most 63 objects, since each holds a PID.
> - an irq -> IRQ-object table sized from the platform's source count, set at boot_devices and cleared at destroy, so irq_device is O(1).
> 
> TEST:
> - A host or model property that each index equals the old scan's answer after every create and free.
> - A bench case, scan-bounds: a budget fills its limit with endpoints. process_create latency, exit-notice delivery and an IRQ round-trip stay within the latency target, and within a fixed ratio of the empty-system baseline.
> - A mutation that skips the index update fails the property.
> The package is now 9 items.
